$comment: Config for scripts/check-issue-queue.mjs -- the steering gate.
WHY THE LABEL NAMES LIVE HERE AND NOT IN THE SCRIPT. The two labels are the maintainer's
steering wheel, and retuning a steering wheel should not be a code change reviewed by the
people being steered. Rename `ready` to `approved`, or point `escapeLabel` at a different
word, and the gate follows without touching a line of JavaScript.
This file lives under scripts/, and .github/workflows/issue-queue.yml carries NO `paths:`
filter, so the job that reads it fires on every pull_request event regardless of which
files changed. That is deliberate and it is copied from pr-review-signal.yml, which
documents the reasoning at length: #3305's gate could not fire on the file it guarded
because that file was in no path filter, and a presence check that can itself be filtered
out is the same defect it is trying to catch. A steering gate is worth even less: a
contributor sweeping for defects on their own initiative can edit this config, or the
gate, in the very PR the gate would have refused.
BOTH LABELS NOW EXIST. Measured 2026-09-02, `gh label list` returns both `ready`
("Maintainer-approved: in scope, wanted now, scoped") and `unqueued` ("Maintainer
waiver"). The earlier note here said neither existed, measured 2026-08-30, and used that
to argue the gate must stay advisory; that argument is spent.
THIS GATE IS STILL NOT A REQUIRED STATUS CHECK. Measured 2026-09-02, the `main` ruleset
(id 11806334) requires exactly three contexts -- `Build + WASM + Rust + Node`, `parity
(in-tree fixtures, committed reference)` and `PR review signal`. `Issue queue` is not
among them, so `enforcing` turns the row RED and blocks no merge. Making it required is
a separate, deliberate act in repository settings, not a side effect of this file.
$readyLabelComment: READY_LABEL: the label on an ISSUE that says the maintainer wants this built.
The measured problem: 608 of one contributor's 743 commits (82%) carried no linked issue,
because the backlog is empty -- 19 open, 698 all-time -- so the agent manufactures its own
work queue by sweeping for defects. A label on an issue is the cheapest possible way for
the maintainer to say `this one', and it costs one click per item rather than one review
$escapeLabelComment: ESCAPE_LABEL: the label on a PULL REQUEST that says `this one is fine unqueued'.
It exists because this gate cannot tell a genuinely urgent drive-by fix -- a release is
broken, main is red, a security report just landed -- from unwanted sweeping. Nothing in
`closingIssuesReferences` carries urgency. Rather than pretend to judge it, the gate hands
the judgement back to a human and records who made it (see `labelAuthorities`).
A gate with no escape hatch gets disabled the first time it is wrong, and a disabled gate
$modeComment: ADVISORY or ENFORCING. Advisory prints the identical verdict and exits 0;
enforcing exits 1. Not defaulted in code: a missing value is a refusal, because
defaulting would let a corrupted config silently downgrade the gate to a no-op.
SHIPPED ADVISORY DELIBERATELY, AND FLIPPED ON 2026-09-02. It shipped advisory
because on the day it landed the highest-volume contributor had 30 open PRs and
no issue carried `ready` yet, so enforcing on day one would have reddened all 30
for a rule that did not exist when they were opened.
THE FLIP IS MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED. On 2026-09-02: 29 open issues, 27 of them
carrying `ready`, so the queue is stocked and the remedy the gate names is one a
contributor can actually take. Of 34 open PRs, 9 pass (6 from the exempt
maintainer, 3 from BIMvoice closing a `ready` issue) and 25 fail, every one of
them NO_LINKED_ISSUE -- they close nothing at all. Not one fails UNQUEUED_WORK,
so no PR is red merely because an issue it links went unlabelled.
25 OF 34 (74%) TURN RED ON THIS COMMIT. That is the cost, stated rather than
discovered. It is not the day-one problem: the queue those PRs need now exists,
the check is not required so nothing is blocked from merging, and the remedy per
PR is one edit -- add `Closes #N` against a `ready` issue, or ask for `unqueued`.
Reverting is the same one-word edit in the other direction.
$labelAuthoritiesComment: WHO IS ALLOWED TO APPLY THE TWO LABELS. This is the half that makes the gate more than a
suggestion, and it is not hypothetical: the contributor this gate is aimed at has
authorAssociation COLLABORATOR (measured on #3540), which means he can apply labels. An
escape label the contributor applies to their own PR defeats the gate completely, and
the same is true of a `ready` label self-applied to a self-filed issue.
IT IS CHECKABLE, AND SO IT IS CHECKED. GitHub's timeline carries LabeledEvent.actor, so
`who applied this label' is a fact, not a guess. Verified live on #3333 (dependabot's own
PR): both `dependencies` and `javascript` come back with actor.login `dependabot`, i.e.
self-applied, which is exactly the shape this rule rejects when it matters.
TWO IDENTITY SPACES, AND THEY DISAGREE. `gh pr list --json author` reports dependabot as
`app/dependabot'; the GraphQL `author { login }' on the SAME PR (#3333) reports
`dependabot'; the REST API reports `dependabot[bot]'. All three spellings are listed in
`exemptLogins` below and the gate normalises all three to the same key, because a login
list that is correct in one API and silently inert in another is a config nobody can
$exemptLoginsComment: WHOSE PRs THIS GATE DOES NOT ADJUDICATE.
The maintainer, because the gate exists to carry HIS direction and a maintainer setting
direction by writing code is setting direction. Requiring him to file an issue, label it
`ready`, and then close it with his own PR is ceremony that steers nobody.
Bots, because they have no work queue to steer. A dependabot bump closes no issue and
never will; failing it teaches contributors that this gate is noise, which is how a gate
ends up disabled. `github-actions` covers the changeset release PR, which likewise closes
ADDING A HUMAN HERE IS A REAL DECISION, not a convenience: it removes that person from
the queue entirely. It is a config change so that it is reviewable, and it is a separate
key from `labelAuthorities` so that `may steer' and `is not steered' stay separable --
